newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MAJOR SPORTS EVENTS TO BE SHOWN FREE ON EU TV.
newsitem.headline: MAJOR SPORTS EVENTS TO BE SHOWN FREE ON EU TV.

text.p: Television viewers in the European Union will be guaranteed free access to major sporting and cultural events in the world of pay-TV under a deal struck on Wednesday by the European Parliament and EU capitals.

In a meeting to settle outstanding differences over how to revise the bloc's so-called "television without frontiers" law, representatives of the two sides agreed EU states must respect other countries' lists of events which must be shown "in the clear."

"This means events such as the World Cup Final, the Olympic Games and the European Football Championship should continue to be available to all for free," British Socialist Euro-MP Carole Tongue said in a statement after the meeting.

The agreement, which must be formally endorsed by the full parliament and the EU's Council of Ministers, means the EU assembly has scored a major goal in securing access for ordinary citizens to free TV sports, after initial resistance by EU governments.
"I've a feeling that we've done something special for the EU citizens," Peter Pex, chairman of the parliament's Culture Committee, told Reuters.

Stonewalled by EU governments, Euro-MPs last year lost their fight to have the law amended to set tougher limits on non-European -- read Hollywood -- films and television programmes shown on the EU's television screens and to have the rules cover new media services that are springing up.

In another concession to the parliament, the European Commission promised on Wednesday to draw up within a year a report on the feasibility of installing so called V-chips in new television sets to help parents screen out violent programmes from their children.
But the Commission's pledge fell short of the parliament's original demand to set a deadline for installing the censors in new television sets.
A spokesman for EU Culture Commissioner Marcelino Oreja said the agreement on the directive lifted a legal uncertainty left by the 1989 law over the broadcast sector.

As things stand, Britain, France and the Belgian region of Flanders adopt lists of sporting events which must be shown free or undecoded when the exclusive rights to the events are snapped up by pay television channels like BSkyB and Canal Plus.
A result of Wednesday's agreement could be that other countries move to set up lists of national and non-national events, EU officials said.
Last July, for example, Germany's Kirch group won a bidding battle for television rights to the 2002 and 2006 World Cup Soccer finals.

In Britain, soccer events like the FA Cup Final, the Scottish FA Cup Final and the World Cup Final are on the list, along with the Derby and Grand National horse races, the Olympic Games, the Wimbledon Tennis Championship and Home Cricket test matches involving England.

On France's list are the summer and winter Olympics, the Tour de France cycle race, European Cup football matches, Five Nations rugby union matches in which the French national team takes part and the French football cup final.
Belgium's Flemish region draws up a new list every year.
